root_motivation: Grounding (failure-derived, 2026-10-05): /healthz on mcphost-1 counts signups (external 14, synthetic 1,759), tenants_claimed (0), and paying_tenants (0) and nothing between -- the tenants table holds created_unix/last_seen_unix (migration 0020), the claim stamps (0034) and plan_since (0006), and no first-call, first-publish, own-tool-call, or second-session stamp (migrations 0002-0071, src/db.rs:170-209). mcphost-deploy measure refuses to report until five tenants are hand-labelled and last wrote on 2026-09-27; funnel-top covers pre-signup demand only. The market test's hypothesis H1 (activation) is therefore unmeasurable. Fix: stamp six activation moments on the tenant at the instant they happen, expose admin.funnel with counts/medians per stage by source class, and put a seven-day funnel block on /healthz, so the market test measures activation without a label ritual.
user_persona: Four (PRD User stories): Operator Joe, who asks admin.funnel {days: 7, source_class: "external"} and sees signups -> first calls -> publishes -> own calls -> returns -> claims, with medians; an agent whose host.usage shows its own milestones so a returning agent can say 'I published on day one'; the morning digest, which gets one admin call for its numbers; and the harness, whose synthetic tenants are stamped too but excluded by source class so panel runs never pollute the external funnel.

additional.second_session_only_watches_the_two_mech: Requirement 2 names exactly bind_session_to_created_tenant and URL-path auth (resolve_path_secret_auth) as second_session_unix's triggers -- not every authenticated-call resolver (resolve_auth/resolve_tenant_key_auth/resolve_session_binding also exist). A stateless client that never echoes Mcp-Session-Id gets a brand-new session id on literally every call, so wiring this into the plain header/tenant_key paths too would fire on a caller's very next ordinary call rather than a real reconnect. mcphost's own typical external-tenant pattern (host.key_rotate mints a personal /u/{secret}/mcp URL) makes the URL-path mechanism the realistic 'reconnect' surface, matching the PRD's literal enumeration.
additional.created_session_id_set_once_at_the_first: bind_session_to_created_tenant fires for both signup and host.redeem; created_session_id is set only the FIRST time a tenant is ever bound (tenant.created_session_id.is_none()) -- a later bind (e.g. host.redeem on a different connection than a handoff signup) is itself evaluated as a candidate second session, never silently overwrites the original creating session.
additional.first_own_call_is_a_same_tenant_distinct: call_published_tool's caller parameter is None for every same-tenant call (direct <ns>.<tool>, or host.tool_call dispatched against the caller's own namespace) and Some(&caller) only for a cross-tenant shared-tool call -- first_own_call_unix is gated on caller.is_none() precisely because that parameter already distinguishes 'self' from 'borrowed' regardless of which function (call_published_tool directly, or via call_shared_tool/host_tool_call) reached it.
additional.k_is_host_wide_over_the_same_window_not_: admin.funnel's k figure (requirement 6) measures INVITERS' own activity (accepted joins per active inviter), a different population than the invitee rows invited narrows admin.funnel's signups/stages to -- so k is computed over every invite_joins row in the same days window regardless of the invited argument's value, generalizing invites_usage_7d's existing per-tenant/fixed-7d k shape to a host-wide figure over an arbitrary window.
additional.by_source_is_never_narrowed_by_the_top_l: admin.funnel's source_class argument narrows signups/stages only; by_source's whole purpose is the breakdown ACROSS every source_class value, so it is built from the signup_source/invited-filtered rows but never the source_class-filtered ones -- narrowing by_source too would make a {source_class: "external"} call's own by_source degenerate to a single external:{...} entry, defeating the field.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is there no funnel number?
five_whys_trace.a: measure refuses to report without five hand-labeled tenants and has not written since 2026-09-27; the nightly chain's preflight has been red (demand_alarm_streak=15) and skips the measure step while red.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the sensor depend on hand labels?
five_whys_trace.a: It was built to classify real vs harness tenants for paid_mrr_usd when synthetic traffic dominated (1,759 synthetic vs 14 external signups); with source_class now stamped at signup, the label gate guards nothing the host doesn't already know.

five_whys_trace.q: Why are there no stages between signup and claim?
five_whys_trace.a: Each onboarding PRD measured its own moment (first-call-gift's AC6 counts remember, invite-links counts k); nobody owns the tenant lifecycle, so the host stores created_unix/last_seen_unix/owner_verified_at/plan_since and nothing in between.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is activation specifically unmeasurable, not just slow to compute?
five_whys_trace.a: The six moments this PRD stamps (first call, first publish, first own-tool call, second session, claim, paid) are never written anywhere -- there is no column, no event log, and no derived read that could answer 'did this tenant activate' even with unlimited compute.

five_whys_trace.q: Why wasn't this caught before the market test needed it?
five_whys_trace.a: With 14 real tenants and a lifecycle nobody owned, activation simply never came up as a question until Joe's market test asked it first -- the deepest actionable level: the host does not record activation, and the tool that should report it is gated on a label ritual and a chain that is red.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the 'second session' rule require a different client (clientInfo), not just a different session id?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- the PRD's own Open Questions table drafts this as 'no' explicitly ('the digest can split by client later'), so second_session_unix compares session ids only, never clientInfo.

ambiguities_resolved.question: When tenant.created_session_id is None (no session was ever recorded at creation -- a stateless client, or a pre-migration tenant), does second_session_unix ever fire at all?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes, via the time-only half of the rule the technical considerations name explicitly ('fall back to the 10-minute rule when no session id exists'): any authenticated call through one of the two named mechanisms at least 10 minutes after created_unix counts, since there's nothing to compare the session id against.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does admin.funnel's by_source breakdown report share/median per bucket, or counts only?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Counts only (signups + a per-stage count per source_class bucket) -- no AC exercises by_source's internal shape, and the top-level stages array already carries share/median for whichever population the caller asked about; by_source's own job is just the cross-class split.
